summary: Branch-office NAT64 translation dropping DNS TCP fallback causing control-plane artifact fetch timeouts in private deploy
description:
Issue summary:
Customer's private deployment (VPC + VPCE) serving a set of branch offices started seeing intermittent model pull failures and control-plane backoffs on 2026-03-10. Impact: serving nodes could not reliably download model shard objects; customer reports failed inference jobs and increased tail latency. Environment: private deploy with VPCE endpoints in us-east-1, branch offices on an IPv6-only overlay using an on-prem NAT64 translator/CGNAT for egress.
Observed behaviour: most DNS queries resolve over UDP; when answers exceed UDP size or include DNSSEC/EDNS0 the stack falls back to TCP53. NAT64 translator silently drops or resets TCP/53 sessions from branch-office subnets. As a result the control plane falls back to DoH/DNS proxies in the corp network which rewrite SVC records and return a private host that fails SNI validation for presigned artifact URLs. This causes 403/502 model shard fetches and repeated retries, triggering service backoff.
Impact: multiple inference pods in the customer's serving fleet reported model pull failures between 05:40-06:20 UTC, causing intermittent 5xx errors and queued requests.
steps_to_reproduce:
1) From an IPv6-only branch host behind the customer's NAT64 appliance, attempt to resolve a large record set (DNSSEC/EDNS0) for artifacts.redwood.internal on UDP.
2) Force a TCP fallback by triggering a truncated UDP response (simulate large TXT or DNSSEC).
3) Observe TCP/53 session: the NAT64 either RSTs the TCP session or drops packets.
4) Attempt model-fetch from a serving node which uses the same branch egress path; observe presigned HEAD/GET returning 403 or 502 and control-plane retries.
5) Repeat with direct VPCE egress (bypass NAT64) and observe normal successful fetches.

investigation_notes:
Initial checks: VPCE health checks were green; S3 presigned logs show requests reaching edge but returning 403 when Host header/certname mismatched. Packet captures from branch NAT64 show TCP/53 sessions being reset by NAT64 device, not by Redwood infrastructure. DNS over UDP truncation pattern present (EDNS0 + large A/AAAA+RRSIG). Hypotheses: (A) NAT64 is performing incorrect address synthesis that drops TCP/53; (B) stateful conntrack table on NAT64 overflowing for long-lived TCP53 attempts; (C) corporate egress firewall performs deep inspection and injects RST for TCP53. Verified: replicable when using customer's NAT64; bypassing NAT64 (direct VPCE egress) resolves issue. Temporary mitigation allowed model pulls when forcing UDP-only queries or increasing UDP buffer on edge; not viable long-term.
Actions taken: asked customer to enable TCP53 passthrough on NAT64 appliance and increase conntrack/timeouts; reproduced in lab with vendor image. Opened INT ticket for infra to add monitoring for DNS-TCP failure rates and control-plane backoff counters. Linked infra PR to add clearer diagnostic logs on DNS fallback path.

2026-03-10 15:02 UTC - Customer (VantageAnalytics): Sent tcpdump and firewall rules. Noted that NAT64 vendor recently patched for other issues.

2026-03-10 18:40 UTC - Ravi Kapoor (SRE): Reproduced in lab using customer's config; NAT64 device resets TCP/53 when conntrack entries exceed threshold. Workaround applied: allow TCP/53 passthrough and increase conntrack table size on customer side.

2026-03-12 09:30 UTC - Ravi Kapoor (SRE): Recommended long-term fix: do not rely on NAT64 translation for VPCE control-plane DNS. Update runbook and add active checks for DNS-TCP fallback rate. Created INT-4421 to implement monitoring and alerting.
2026-03-12 12:00 UTC - Customer (VantageAnalytics): Confirmed increased stability after workaround; no model-pull failures observed in last 24h.
resolution: Applied customer-implemented workaround: enabled TCP/53 passthrough and increased NAT64 conntrack table/timeouts on branch appliance. Confirmed control-plane artifact fetches successful when bypassing NAT64 or with TCP passthrough enabled. Follow-up actions: 1) internal PR to add DNS-TCP fallback metrics and alert (INT-4421). 2) Confluence runbook updated with NAT64 checklist and recommended VPCE bypass architecture for branch overlays. 3) Recommend customer adopt split-dns where VPCE queries go to Redwood resolvers over VPCE instead of egressing through NAT64.
